response.sql: SELECT f.orderslink, o.mktnote, AVG(f.rebrate) as avg_rebrate, SUM(f.rebtotal) as total_rebate FROM fees f INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.mktnote ORDER BY total_rebate DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: "Ignoring missing values" means using SQL's standard aggregation behavior where AVG() and SUM() skip NULL values in their calculations, rather than excluding rows with NULL rebrate or rebtotal from the input.

The database supports NULLS LAST syntax in ORDER BY (PostgreSQL, Oracle, etc.). MySQL and some other databases require alternative syntax: ORDER BY CASE WHEN total_rebate IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, total_rebate DESC

alternatives.interpretation: "Ignoring missing values" means to exclude fee records where either rebrate or rebtotal are NULL before computing the average and sum.
alternatives.sql: SELECT f.orderslink, o.mktnote, AVG(f.rebrate) as avg_rebrate, SUM(f.rebtotal) as total_rebate FROM fees f INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009 AND f.rebrate IS NOT NULL AND f.rebtotal IS NOT NULL GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.mktnote ORDER BY total_rebate DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
